title: Tansy and Bobo's Giggle Seeds
markdown:
Tansy the squirrel lived in a burrow as snug as a bug in a rug, deep in the Whispering Woods. Her fur was the colour of warm toast, and her tail twitched faster than you could say acorn. She loved shiny things: dewdrops that winked on spiderwebs, pebbles from the brook as smooth as a sleepy kitten’s nose. She also kept nut stashes under roots and in hollows, and some mornings she counted them twice, then once more, just to be sure.

Her very best friend was Bobo. Bobo was a little bat, fuzzy and round, with wings like dark velvet that sparkled like polished jet. He did not only fly. He zipped and zoomed on a broomstick no bigger than a thumb, a tiny broom that made a soft happy whirr-whirr. His grin could melt a grumpy cloud into sunshine.

One bright bubbly morning, as the sun stretched golden fingers over the tallest oak, Tansy was polishing her favourite acorn. It gleamed like a tiny brown jewel. Suddenly a shimmer-swish of sparkly light whooshed past her twitching nose. A tiny seed, no bigger than a ladybug, glowed like a captured star. Before she could blink, more shimmer-swish seeds tumbled from the blue sky, landing with soft pings on the moss. They sparkled with a gentle mysterious light.

“Bobo. Come quick. Look at this,” chattered Tansy, scooping the starry seeds. Bobo, who had been practising loops over the berry bushes, zoomed down, his whirr-whirr growing closer. “Moon seeds,” he chirped, dark eyes wide. “My Grandma told stories. She said they bloom with sparkly magic when the time is just right. We have to plant them before the moon starts to get sleepy.”

Tansy’s fluffy tail gave a worried twitch. “What if they don’t bloom, Bobo?” she whispered. She thought of empty earth, of waiting for nothing, of a stash that never filled.

Bobo nudged her with his fuzzy head. His velvety ears brushed her cheek. “We’ll plant them. We’ll find the very best spot in the whole Whispering Woods.” With a determined hop and a tiny whizz, they scurried to a sunny patch beside a babbling brook. The brook sang a gurgly song as it skipped over smooth stones. With nimble paws, and Bobo’s broomstick acting as a perfect little shovel, they tucked each moon seed into the soft dark earth. They patted the soil down ever so gently. A ladybug sat on a pebble and watched as if this were important work.

Then they waited. The sun climbed high, warm and bright, and then it dipped, painting the clouds in orange and soft pink. The ground where they had planted stayed just ground. Nothing happened. Not a sprout. Not a shimmer.

“Oh dear,” sighed Tansy, her tail drooping like a wilting flower. “They’re not growing. They’re just sleeping.” She felt a strong urge to leave them. “It’s no use. Let’s go play with the shiny pebbles instead.” She almost turned toward the brook, toward things that already gleamed.

Bobo circled high, his broomstick making a soft encouraging hum. “Sometimes growing takes a little extra help. Maybe they need to hear a happy sound. Something to wake them up.”

So they tried singing. Tansy sang her bubbliest squirrel song, about scampering and collecting nuts. Bobo sang his buzziest bat tune, full of night-sky adventures. They even told the seeds the silliest jokes they knew. “Why did the squirrel cross the road?” Tansy asked the ground. “To get to the nut-shop.” She giggled a little herself. Bobo added, “What do you call a sleeping bull? A bulldozer.” Still the moon seeds stayed stubbornly tucked in their earthy beds. A bee drifted past, unimpressed. The brook kept gurgling, as if it knew a secret and would not share it yet.

“This is trickier than I thought,” admitted Bobo, landing softly beside Tansy. He tapped his chin with a tiny paw. “Grandma said moon seeds bloom when they hear the most wonderful, most magical sound in the whole wide world.”

Tansy tilted her head. “What sound is that?”

Bobo wiggled his nose. “A giggle.”

“A giggle?” Tansy frowned. “How do we make them giggle if we aren’t giggling? My tummy feels all wiggly.”

Suddenly Bobo zoomed up, then spun on his broomstick like a little dizzy dervish. He wobbled and dipped, swooped and swayed, doing a funny broomstick dance that looked like jelly on a trampoline. Whee. Whoosh. Wobble-wobble-splat. He landed with a gentle thump, upside down, fuzzy legs sticking straight up like tiny twigs.

Tansy stared. Her mouth opened. A tiny snort of surprise escaped. Then a chuckle bubbled up. Then she burst into a huge happy tinkling giggle. “Heeheehee. Oh, Bobo, you look so funny.” Her whole body shook with the delight of it. The laugh hopped from her whiskers to the brook, and the brook seemed to laugh back.

As Tansy’s giggles danced on the soft breeze, the ground began to shimmer with a soft inner light. Tiny sprouts, like little green wishes, popped from the earth. On top of each sprout a tiny bud unfurled, opening petals that sparkled with moonlight magic. The air smelled sweet and warm, like honey and moonbeams. The soft petals felt like cool velvet against her nose as she leaned in.

Tansy gasped, clapping her paws. “They’re blooming. They’re really, truly blooming.” The moon flowers twinkled like sleepy stars that had fallen from the sky, filling the little clearing with a dream-like glow. One blossom nodded toward Bobo’s broom as if to thank the upside-down landing.

Bobo righted himself with a happy whizz, his grin wider than ever. “The very best magic is a happy giggle.”

Tansy looked at Bobo, then at the twinkling moon flowers. She snuggled close, warm all over. The flutter in her tummy had gone, replaced by the bubbly joy of a friend who would plant, wait, sing, and fall over on purpose. They sat side by side, watching their moon flowers twinkle under the star-dusted evening sky, the brook still singing, the seeds no longer a secret.
